scope: The exact source commit passes the complete platform-applicable deis-provider-driver test suite, including release-index validation and verified installation behavior, plus strict all-target lint on Linux, macOS, and Windows with the repository-pinned Rust toolchain.

test.note: Unix installation-root ownership/mode and process-group tests are enabled.
Seven platform-applicable installer tests and two Windows Job Object tests are enabled; Unix-only root-mode, process-group, and environment tests are not compiled.

checks.note: Strict lint rejected three Windows-only set_readonly(false) calls under clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false.

priorFailedAttempts.cause: The Windows cleanup path used the cross-platform Permissions::set_readonly(false) API. Its Windows behavior was tested, but strict lint correctly rejected an API whose accidental Unix use would create an unsafe permission change.

checks.note: Compilation failed before tests because std::os::windows::fs::PermissionsExt and its attribute methods do not exist in Rust 1.96.0.

priorFailedAttempts.cause: The first fix assumed a Windows std permission extension that Rust does not provide; Linux and macOS builds could not expose this target-specific compile error.

limitations: The release-index fixture is synthetic; this evidence does not prove a real Wrangler, EdgeOne, Deislet, or other provider release archive.
The installer validates bytes, paths, files, component membership, and content-addressed publication, but release signing, trust-root rotation, revocation, and transparency are not implemented.
On Windows, read-only file attributes are verified but no service-account DACL is configured or validated; this is not an equivalent authorization boundary.
Control has no durable installed-release registry or production dispatcher that selects the current host release and re-verifies its full tree before every driver execution.
No live provider account is used, and this evidence does not certify any backend against Edge Canon.
